newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parties' ranking before parliamentary polls.
newsitem.headline: Polish parties' ranking before parliamentary polls.

text.p: A poll by the private Demoskop institute showed on Tuesday the the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the opposition Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) are supported by 21 percent each.
The poll clearly confirmed results of an earlier survey which showed June's trip of Pope John Paul II to Poland had only small impact on electoral preferences.
Following is a ranking of Polish political parties according to the five most recent public opinion polls.
AWS - The Solidarity Electoral Action, an opposition electoral bloc of more than 30 small right-wing parties led by the Solidarity trade union.
SLD - the Democratic Left Alliance, the ex-communist group and the larger partner in the ruling leftist coalition.
PSL - The Polish Peasant Party, the smaller partner in the government coalition.
UW - The Union for Freedom, a right-centrist group, the biggest opposition party in parliament.
ROP - The Movement for Reconstruction of Poland, a non-parliamentary group, advocating patriotic, anti-communist and often populist values.
UP - The Union of Labour, a leftist opposition party. KPEiR - The National Pensioners' Party, a party lobbying pensioners' interests.
CBOS - public, Poland's biggest polling institution.
OBOP - controlled by the state-owned television.
PBS - private, preparing polls for the Rzeczpospolita daily.
